lines.text: Every few decades, a profession is rewritten.
1928. Penicillin. 1953. The double helix. 2003. The human genome.
2024. A Nobel Prize, for AI that predicts the shape of proteins.
And 2026. The year AI enters every pharmacy classroom in India.
Medicine is a search through ten to the sixty possible molecules.
For a century, we searched by hand: fifteen years, billions of dollars, a single medicine.
Then AI learned to read chemistry. To a model, paracetamol is eighteen characters.
AlphaFold predicted the structure of over two hundred million proteins, each with its own confidence score.
A message-passing neural network screened more than a hundred million molecules, and discovered a new antibiotic.
Today, a single Phase III trial generates 3.6 million data points.
The FDA has reviewed over five hundred drug submissions built with AI.
And India, which makes one in five of the world’s generic medicines, is ready to lead what comes next.
The PCI has written that future into the B.Pharm. NEP 2020. From 2026–27.
Semester one, Python Programming: a student writes her first line of code.
Two, Biostatistics and Data Analytics: she proves bioequivalence, a 90% confidence interval inside 80 to 125 percent.
Three, Machine Learning: she predicts solubility from molecular descriptors, before a single gram is made.
Five, Innovation and Startups: idea, prototype, pilot.
Six, AI in Pharmaceutical Sciences and Computer-Aided Drug Design: she docks molecules into a target and ranks them by binding energy.
Seven, AI in Clinical Practice: she detects drug-safety signals across thousands of reports.
Eight, Ethics of AI: she learns to prove a model is fair, explainable and safe.
Four years. One pharmacist who can do all of this.
And here’s the beautiful part. Every college can teach this. Starting this semester.
Campus Champ. Built for this syllabus, unit by unit. On one idea: blended learning.
Before class, students meet the topic on their phones: a calm voice, a live animation, in Kannada, Hindi, Hinglish or English.
In class, your teacher does what only a teacher can. Explains. Questions. Inspires.
After class, students run real Python on their own phones. Every answer checked instantly.
And your teacher sees which concept the class finds hardest, and begins the next class right there.
No lab to build. No textbook to buy. Code stays in English, exactly as the exam needs. NEP 2020, in every classroom.
Two hours a week becomes a learning experience that never stops. Live in thirty days.
And it has already begun. Over a hundred pharmacy students in Bagalkot learn this way today.
One day, someone will write the story of how India’s pharmacists learned AI.
It will name the first colleges that made it happen.
Colleges whose students went on to design medicines, protect patients, and build companies of their own.
This year, the first Founding Partner colleges begin that story.
Penicillin. DNA. The genome. AI.
History remembers those who go first.
Let it remember your college.
